source.title: Optimal Online Contention Resolution Schemes via Ex-Ante Prophet Inequalities

background: Online contention resolution schemes (OCRS) are rounding procedures for random active sets subject to feasibility constraints. They were introduced as a generic way to convert fractional solutions into online feasible selections, and they now form a bridge between prophet inequalities, stochastic probing, posted pricing, and submodular optimization. A parallel viewpoint is the ex-ante prophet inequality, where the benchmark is a relaxation that constrains each element's selection probability before values are realized. Lee and Singla showed that, in random and fixed arrival orders, optimal ex-ante prophet inequalities can be used to design optimal OCRSs. Will Ma's problem asks whether this equivalence survives under an oblivious adversarial order. This adversary chooses the order without seeing realizations, so it is weaker than an adaptive adversary but stronger than random order. The question is structural: are OCRSs and ex-ante prophet inequalities still the same object in this intermediate model, or can their guarantees diverge?
full_statement: Let $N$ be a ground set and let $\mathcal F\subseteq2^N$ be a downward-closed feasibility family, such as a matroid. An ex-ante fractional point $x\in P_{\mathcal F}$ specifies activation probabilities: each element $i$ is active independently with probability $x_i$, and active elements are revealed online. An online contention resolution scheme must decide immediately whether to accept each revealed active element while maintaining an accepted set in $\mathcal F$. A scheme is $c$-selectable if every element $i$ is accepted with probability at least $c x_i$, possibly under assumptions on the arrival order. An ex-ante prophet inequality instead assigns independent values to elements and compares an online selection policy with an ex-ante relaxation that maximizes expected value subject to marginal probabilities in $P_{\mathcal F}$. Lee and Singla show that, in fixed-order and random-order models, optimal ex-ante prophet inequalities can be converted into optimal OCRSs. The open problem is whether this equivalence continues to hold when the order is chosen adversarially but obliviously to the active set and values: for every feasibility family and every target guarantee, does an ex-ante prophet inequality in the oblivious-adversarial-order model imply an OCRS with the same guarantee, and conversely?
known_results: Feldman, Svensson, and Zenklusen introduced OCRSs and showed their broad applicability to Bayesian selection, posted pricing, stochastic probing, and submodular objectives. Lee and Singla proved optimal OCRS guarantees via reductions to ex-ante prophet inequalities, including an optimal $1/2$ OCRS for matroids and a $(1-1/e)$ random-order contention-resolution scheme for matroids. Their work answers a conceptual question: prophet inequalities can be used to design optimal OCRSs, not just the other way around. However, their reductions are order-sensitive. Fixed orders and uniformly random orders are covered, while the course-note problem identifies the oblivious-adversarial-order case as unresolved. In this model the adversary chooses the order before seeing activations or values, so it is weaker than an adaptive adversary, but it can still arrange elements to stress the rounding scheme. No source-checked theorem was found that either extends the Lee-Singla equivalence to this intermediate model or gives a separating feasibility system.

where_posed.text: Posed in Will Ma's Online Resource Allocation course notes, Appendix C, Open Problems about Online Contention Resolution Schemes, Problem 1.

progress.summary: Equivalence is known for random and fixed orders. The oblivious-adversarial-order model remains the missing intermediate case.

links.title: Lee and Singla, ex-ante prophet inequalities and OCRS

counterexample_rationale: A separation might be witnessed by a small feasibility system and fractional point, but proving optimality of both sides for that example may be nontrivial.
alphaevolve_rationale: Automated search can test small set systems and orders for gaps between OCRS and ex-ante values. General proofs likely require structural reductions.

literature.synthesis: OCRSs began as online analogues of offline contention resolution schemes and quickly became a unifying tool for Bayesian selection. Their role is to round independent activations while preserving marginal acceptance probabilities under online feasibility constraints. Ex-ante prophet inequalities use a value objective, but after conditioning on quantiles they often expose the same marginal-rounding structure. Lee and Singla's key insight was that ex-ante prophet inequalities can be used to obtain optimal OCRSs, reversing the earlier direction where OCRSs implied prophet inequalities. The open problem asks whether this symmetry is robust to an oblivious adversarial order. The difficulty is that ex-ante prophet policies may use value thresholds and distributional information in a way that is harder to translate into value-free selectability when the element order is worst-case but fixed independently of realizations. A positive solution would unify the two objects across the main order models. A negative solution would identify a genuinely new separation between value-aware selection and contention-resolution rounding.

reviewed.result: Introduces OCRSs and proves constant-factor schemes with applications to Bayesian selection and stochastic probing.

reviewed.ref: Euiwoong Lee, Sahil Singla, 'Optimal Online Contention Resolution Schemes via Ex-Ante Prophet Inequalities', ESA 2018
reviewed.result: Proves optimal OCRS guarantees via ex-ante prophet inequalities for fixed and random order settings.

reviewed.result: Gives the foundational $1/2$ matroid prophet inequality and connects online selection under matroid constraints to mechanism design.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Try small feasibility families first: rank-1, partition matroids, and tiny non-matroid downward-closed systems. Compute the best ex-ante prophet guarantee and best OCRS selectability under fixed oblivious orders, then look for equality-preserving transformations.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A positive solution must define the precise order model and give a reduction that preserves guarantees for every downward-closed family or for the stated class, such as matroids. The proof must not accidentally assume random order or an order chosen after seeing the active set. A counterexample must use the same feasibility family, activation polytope, and order model on both sides: it should prove an ex-ante prophet guarantee and a strictly smaller OCRS upper bound, or vice versa, under oblivious adversarial order. Computational searches over small set systems should report exact LPs or dynamic programs for both quantities; simulation alone is not enough because small gaps may be artifacts of discretization.
